findings.claim: In EventManager (around line 118-119), mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, then `.integration` is read without a guard. When evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty this throws a TypeError, which breaks the Google Meet to Daily fallback.

verifier.reason: At packages/core/EventManager.ts:118-119, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` is undefined when destinationCalendar is null, undefined or an empty array. Calendar.d.ts:171 allows those values. `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is then read without `?.`, so when evt.location is Google Meet it throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Daily. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and was safe.

findings.claim: In GoogleCalendarService createEvent() and updateEvent(), mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar. It is undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty, which causes a null reference.

verifier.reason: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100-103 and 198-199, a null or empty destinationCalendar falls back to `[]`, so mainHostDestinationCalendar is just undefined. Every read of it uses optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` at lines 122 and 228), and the code falls back to the organizer's email, so nothing throws.

findings.claim: Several places destructure the first element of an array (`[first] = array`) and access its properties without guarding against undefined.

verifier.reason: packages/core/EventManager.ts:118-119 does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no `?.`. findings.claim: In GoogleCalendarService updateEvent (line ~256) and deleteEvent (line ~317), the fallback `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it never matches. As a result, updateEvent sends an undefined calendarId, and deleteEvent falls back to 'primary' instead of the booking's destination calendar.

verifier.reason: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256 and :315-317 only run `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it is comparing against null, undefined or "", and it won't match any real calendar ID. As a result, updateEvent passes `calendarId: undefined` (line 261) and deleteEvent falls back to "primary" (line 322), where the old code used `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`.

findings.claim: In Google createEvent, selectedCalendar can be undefined when no destination calendar matches credentialId, but later code passes it directly as calendarId (e.g., calendar.events.patch).

verifier.reason: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147-149, selectedCalendar is `destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, so it can be undefined. Line 154 falls back to `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the hangout-link `calendar.events.patch` at line 168 passes the bare `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, so that patch call gets undefined. findings.claim: Google createEvent picks the target calendar only by credentialId match, so destination calendars with a null credentialId go to 'primary' instead of the selected calendar.

verifier.reason: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (patch lines 80-88), Google createEvent picks the calendar only with `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` and otherwise uses "primary". EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents (patch lines 358-363) sends destinations whose credentialId is null to `createEvent(c, event)` for each credential of the matching integration type, so nothing matches and the event goes to 'primary'. findings.claim: In handleNewBooking (lines ~1063-1079), evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. findings.claim: The organization slug condition in organizations/create.handler.ts (line ~151) is inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`. findings.claim:
The loadUsers rewrite in handleNewBooking.ts changes behavior:
- An empty dynamicUserList throws a plain Error (500) instead of reaching the 404 path.
- Prisma errors are re-thrown as 400 with the raw message.
- Other errors are swallowed.
- The organization slug select is dropped while IsFixedAwareUser still declares it.

verifier.reason: In the patched loadUsers (handleNewBooking.ts:710-763), an empty dynamicUserList throws a plain Error that the catch turns into a generic 500 "Unable to load users". Prisma known-request errors are re-thrown as 400 with the raw message, other errors lose their message and become that generic 500, and the `organization: { select: { slug } }` select is gone even though IsFixedAwareUser (line 355) still declares `organization: { slug: string }`. One detail is overstated: before the patch an empty list did not clearly reach the 404 at lines 781-798, and nothing in this file reads organization.slug.

findings.claim: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents (lines ~338-380) loops over each destinationCalendar entry but passes the full event with all destination calendars to each integration, and does not forward externalId to the provider. Providers that read destinationCalendar[0] (Office365, Lark, CalDAV) therefore create every host's event on the first host's calendar.

verifier.reason: EventManager.ts:339-370 loops over each destination but passes the whole `event` to `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. CalendarManager.ts:236 then calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` and only copies externalId into the returned result (line 267), never to the provider. Office365 (CalendarService.ts:73-77), Lark (lines 128-142) and CalDAV (lib/CalendarService.ts:156) all use `destinationCalendar[0]`, while only Google selects its calendar by credentialId.

findings.claim: LarkCalendarService (lines 128, 164, 192, 237) uses event.destinationCalendar[0], which targets the first calendar even in collective flows with multiple destination calendars and credentials.

verifier.reason: In packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts at lines 128 and 164, createEvent and createAttendees always use `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`. They ignore the credentialId that CalendarManager.ts now passes, unlike the Google service, which matches the calendar by credentialId. As a result, EventManager's per-destination loop writes every Lark host's event to the first host's calendar ID. updateEvent and deleteEvent (lines 192 and 237) use externalCalendarId first and fall back to [0] only when it is missing.

findings.claim: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (Lark, Office365, packages/lib CalendarService) still declare createEvent(event) without credentialId. packages/lib CalendarService also selects only the first destination calendar at line 156.

verifier.reason: packages/types/Calendar.d.ts now declares createEvent(event, credentialId), and only Google uses the id to find the matching destination (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147-149). Lark (larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:125), Office365 (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72) and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:125 still take only the event, and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156 takes the first destination calendar. The short signatures still compile in TypeScript, but EventManager.ts now calls createEvent once per destination, so for any host after the first these services look up the main host's calendar id and either create nothing (CalDAV filter) or call the wrong calendar.

findings.claim: Office365CalendarService updateEvent lacks the externalCalendarId parameter and deleteEvent lacks the event and externalCalendarId parameters required by the Calendar interface, so update and delete always use the default calendar path.

verifier.reason: In packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, `updateEvent(uid, event)` (line 94) and `deleteEvent(uid)` (line 111) take no externalCalendarId, and both always call the default-calendar URL `/me/calendar/events/${uid}` (lines 96, 113). findings.claim: In EventManager updateAllCalendarEvents (lines ~511-542), credential can remain undefined when reference.credentialId points to a missing credential and the DB fallback finds nothing. updateEvent(credential, ...) is then called and throws, which turns the update into a failure result for every calendar in the booking.

findings.claim: When cancelling a recurring booking, the series-delete block sits inside the per-reference loop but does not depend on the reference. It deletes the series N times using only the first calendar reference, so other hosts' copies are never deleted.

verifier.reason: In handleCancelBooking.ts:445-465 the recurring-series block runs once for every calendar reference in the loop over `bookingCalendarReference` that starts at line 420, but it never uses that reference or `calendarCredential`. findings.claim: In handleCancelBooking lines 449-458, the code ignores the current reference and uses updBooking.references.find(). Each updated booking therefore contributes at most one _calendar reference, so only the first host's event is deleted. The branch also uses bookingToDelete.user.credentials, dropping a DB-fetched team credential.

verifier.reason: In handleCancelBooking.ts:449-458 the recurring branch is inside the per-reference loop, but it never uses `reference`. findings.claim: Each team member's Google event is inserted with the main host as organizer and the same conferenceData requestId.

findings.claim: The organizer email on every host's Google event is destinationCalendar[0].externalId (the main host's calendar), even for other hosts' calendars.

findings.claim: In createAllCalendarEvents, the else branch (line ~380) calls createEvent(c, event) without passing destination.externalId, so externalCalendarId is undefined on that path.
